subject: railgunCarrier
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: six-wheeled railgun carrier braced on stabiliser legs.
Style: low-poly sci-fi military.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single, efficient TypeScript module for the vehicle, keeping it compact and correct. Since this is a vehicle rather than a creature, I'll go with a static model and skip the joint hierarchy entirely for simplicity.

Now I'm working out the vehicle's dimensions in meters—roughly 11m long, 3m wide, with six wheels (0.75m radius) arranged across three axles, a forward-facing cab, and a rear-mounted railgun turret braced by deployed stabiliser outriggers touching the ground alongside the wheels.

Designing wheel assembly...

For colors I'm planning a camo paint scheme for the hull using patches of olive drab tones, and sketching out which SDK utilities to import—patches, mottle, countershade, paint, noise, and a glow kit—plus considering SVG decals like stars for extra detail.

Now I'm designing the chassis structure: setting wheel and hull dimensions so fenders clear the wheels properly, and planning to build the main hull as a lofted shape with stations defining width and height along its length for the sloped front profile.

Plotting the hull outline as a low deck profile with a raised cab section near the nose, sketching coordinates to get the sloped windshield transition right.

I'm planning the fender details too — small boxy slabs above each wheel with mudflaps, positioned outside the hull sides where the wheels sit, since smoothing and coloring will just use the default painted patches.

Next I'm working out axle housings as dark cylinders spanning the width at wheel height, plus a differential bulge and suspension arm boxes. For the cab, I'm defining the windshield as a sloped front face with a decal plane, sketching the profile points for the cab's angled nose and roofline.

Now I'm adding cab details like roof light bars with amber glow, antenna whips, mirrors, headlights, bumper, tow hooks, and armored grille plating. Then I'm planning the rear railgun mount: a turret ring and base, with parallel rail barrels elevated to clear the cab roof and point forward.

Writing barrel geometry helper...

Now I'm working out the gun pitch angle (9°) and its direction/up vectors, positioning the trunnion pivot relative to the turret ring and checking vertical clearance of the barrel over the cab roof as it extends forward.

Still designing railgun geometry...

Working through the geometry so the breech doesn't collide with the capacitor bank — checking the gun's pivot offset and pitch angle to compute the rear end's z-position, then placing capacitor cylinder rows behind it with enough clearance.

I'm also planning the rear hull details: a ladder, tail lights, bumper, generator vents with grille texture, and figuring out where to put outrigger stabilizer legs relative to the wheel axle positions so they don't overlap the wheels.

I'll place mid legs at z=0.6 to fit in the wide wheel gaps, giving four legs total between the front and rear positions. Each leg combines a horizontal mounting beam with a hydraulic-style assembly: an outer sleeve cylinder, an inner piston cylinder, and a wide circular foot pad at the base.

For the pad I'll add a low cylinder resting right at ground level, plus a diagonal brace rod connecting hull to sleeve for structural detail, ribs, bolt clusters, a hydraulic hose, hazard-stripe texture on the beam, a ball-joint sphere on top of the pad, and a dark rubber disc underneath -- mirrored across the vehicle. I'm also planning hull mounting plates for the legs and side details like toolboxes, a fuel tank, a ladder, and side skirts, along with decals such as an insignia roundel, a stenciled "RG-06" serial, and hazard stripes on the side panels.

Adding a caution high-voltage label using the monospace font for the SVG text, then working out the camo paint pattern for the hull with a custom paint function that blends in mud coloring toward the lower areas using noise, and lightens the top surfaces based on normal direction.

I'm defining a steel paint with grainy noise and a sheen effect for metal parts, plus a darker gunmetal paint for armor pieces, while keeping flat colors minimal to stay under the 64-color limit. Now I'm starting the wheel construction function, beginning with the tire geometry as a cylinder.

Still building tread geometry and lug nut placement...

Still placing wheel details...

For hull armor, I'm adding appliqué plates on the sides with bolt rows, using a generic bolt helper that orients hex-cylinder bolts via a quaternion aligned to the surface normal, merging everything into the hull's geometry at the end.

Switching from quaternions to simple Euler rotations per axis for the bolt orientation to keep things consistent with the build style, then moving on to adding a sensor mast with a radar dish on the cab roof, using a lathe profile to shape the dish.

Positioning the dish higher to clear the rails with enough margin from the roof edge, then turning to the roof light bar placement near the cab's sloped front, giving it an amber glow and planning an IR spotlight alongside it. Now I'm working out headlight boxes on the sloped nose face, fitting them within the appropriate height range.

Placing the headlights symmetrically with pale yellow glow and dark bezels, then adding a textured grille with louvers between them, a striped bumper with a hazard decal, tow hooks, and a winch drum with cable on the bumper. I'm also planning hazard and number decals for the hull sides, factoring in the hull's thickness for positioning.

For the side panels, I'm orienting the decal planes so the artwork reads correctly when viewed from outside, then adding camo paint with cheap procedural panel-line seams using fractional UV coordinates based on surface normal direction.

Now I'm listing the texture set needed: windshield glass, hazard stripes, roundel insignia, a stencil "RG-06" callout, grille louvers, a high-voltage warning label with lightning bolt, a glowing cyan turret status display, and a "MK-IX RAIL" gun marking — skipping flags, runes, and mud splatter decals as unnecessary.

Beyond textures, I'm adding small physical details: a rear mini ladder, handrail posts around the deck edges, olive jerry cans mounted on the left side, and thin whip antennas with bent tips at the rear corners, while skipping tow chains and a spare wheel to keep things simple.

I'm checking ground contact math -- making sure the wheel treads, tyre radius, and hull clearance pads all sit just barely above y=0 without sinking into the ground, then adding a drive shaft rod and dark chassis frame rails running under the hull for undercarriage detail.

Now I'm moving up to the turret: positioning hydraulic elevation cylinders from the turret to the gun cradle, building cheek plates for the trunnion pivot, and laying out the turret body as a short cylindrical ring sitting on the deck topped with a box.

Still placing gun components...

Adding muzzle shielding at the end of the barrel with a glowing core, plus recoil cylinder details underneath the cradle with sleeves and pistons.

Now I'm placing a capacitor box above the breech and a row of coil-capacitor cylinders along the top of the shroud. I'm working out the transform matrix for the gun frame, rotating about the X axis by the negative pitch angle so local gun-part coordinates map correctly into the model's world space before applying translations.

I'm defining helper functions: one for building gun-local geometry and applying the gun matrix before adding the part, and another for plane-based textured labels that need rotation to face outward correctly on the shroud. I'll just add roughly a hundred individual parts rather than merging by color, and set up a general model-space helper for positioning and rotating geometry directly.

Writing imports and setup...

Writing geometry helpers...

For parts without an explicit joint, I'm defaulting them to attach near the model's root origin, and confirming static props without bones are fine as long as a root is returned. I'm also adding a flat-shading option to the part helper, defaulting it true for low-poly cylinders and spheres.

Now I'm setting up merge arrays for repeated details like bolts, treads, lugs, and spokes, using a small accumulator helper to collect geometry, position, and rotation before merging. I'm writing a bolt-generator function that creates small hex cylinders, rotates them based on which axis they sit on, and offsets them outward from the surface so they look embedded in the part.

Defining color palette and camo pattern...

Still defining material shaders...

Now I'm sketching out the SVG textures for windshield glass with its diagonal glare and frame, a hazard-stripe pattern using rotated black rectangles, and starting on a roundel design.

Designing more icon details — the warning label, gun label, and screen SVGs — then moving into the actual assembly code, starting with the hull extrusion profile points.

Still shaping the hull outline...

Now I'm positioning the side windows along the cab's sloped profile, sizing and centering them to fit between the front slope and door region, then adding door seam lines, handle, and mirror arm details, and considering where to place the roundel on the hull side given the shallow door height.

I'm working out placement for hull decals and markings — stencils, hazard stripes, warning labels, and a roundel — checking against wheel arches and leg beam attachment points to avoid overlaps, and adjusting the stencil's position along the z-axis to clear the beams.

Still building fenders and mudflaps...

Now adding the axle geometry: a cylindrical shaft with a differential sphere at the rear, plus leaf-spring suspension packs and shocks at each wheel position, and a walking beam linking the tandem rear axles.

For the stabilizer legs, I'm positioning the mounting blocks on the hull sides, extending outrigger beams outward, and adding cylindrical sleeves for the deployment mechanism.

Still placing piston, foot pad, ball joint, and diagonal brace geometry...

Still plotting hose geometry... I'm also planning bolts, tail lights, rear plate, ladder, and towing eye placements, plus checking that leg mounts line up correctly with the hull's rear extent.

Now I'm laying out the capacitor bank as a row of small cylinders with glowing cyan caps mounted on a frame box, connecting them with cables that sweep toward the gun breech, and adding generator vent boxes on the open deck space between the turret and cab.

Next I'm placing ammo magazine racks as paired boxes flanking the gun axis, adding camo equipment containers with hazard stripes on the mid-deck, and starting to shape the turret body using an extruded profile with a sloped front face.

The turret details come next: a hatch cylinder on top, a periscope, side armor plates with bolts, and angled smoke grenade launcher tubes mounted near the front corners, with decal screens planned for the side faces instead of the rear.

Now I'm positioning the gun mount cheeks as steel boxes flanking the turret, sized and placed to align with the trunnion cylinder that serves as the pivot axis for the gun mount, checking that the cheek bottoms and gun shroud heights line up correctly for the breech's pitch rotation.

I need to verify the breech clearance along the pitch angle, checking that the lowered rear of the breech stays above the turret roof and cap bank at various depths — comparing local y-offsets from the trunnion pivot against the turret's top surface height as it slopes toward the rear.

Since there's a slight conflict near the slope transition, I'm raising the trunnion pivot height to 4.1 and making the cheeks taller to compensate, then rechecking the breech bottom clearance at the rear — that comes out fine now. I also need to verify the gun's clearance against the cab roof at mid-depth, and work out dimensions for the saddle/prongs supporting the barrel, before tallying up the total height at full elevation and muzzle extension.

Overall vehicle height is coming out around 6 meters, which feels large but is plausible for a heavy railgun carrier, so I'm fine leaving it. I'm reconsidering the barrel pitch angle, dropping it to 7° and recomputing trig values, then re-adjusting the pivot position and rechecking the breech bottom against the turret profile near the rear — it's marginal, so I bump the pivot up slightly to 4.05 to be safe, reasoning that minor overlaps won't be visually obvious anyway. Finally I recheck the cab roof clearance with the new pivot height and confirm there's enough room for a 0.9m saddle, then move on to thinking about the windscreen.

Now I'm sketching out the saddle mount as two prong boxes flanking the gun with a small cradle cushion on top, and noting the rear travel lock is fine as-is. Then I start laying out the gun's internal components in local coordinates: the breech box, a steel top module, small coil-cap cylinders along the barrel axis with glowing end discs, and a rear breech plate with a hatch detail, while considering adding a power cable feed near the back.

Still defining gun geometry...

This confirms the right vector matches drawing's x-axis mapping to -z, so text reads normally for that face. Checking the -x side similarly: with the rotation applied, the normal points along -x and drawing-x maps to +z, with the viewer's right vector computing to +x.

Now I'm working out the recoil buffer and rail placements—figuring out rail box dimensions and center position along the gun's length, noting overlap with the shroud, and setting the rail color.

Adding top caps, inner glow strips, ceramic insulators between rails, and ring clamp positions...

Adding muzzle blast diffuser plates, a glowing cyan core between the rails, warning stripe accents, and recoil cylinder pistons under the gun...

Adding more cab details now — hood vents, headlight bezels, grille and bumper with tow hooks and winch, then roof components like a light bar, hatch, mast with dish, antenna whips with bent rods, a rear cab rack, roof rack rails, and a sun visor box positioned above the windshield.

Now I'm placing the side mirrors with arm and mirror boxes, adding a vertical exhaust stack with heat shield and cap cone behind the cab, and starting on the deck hand components.

I'm then adding small posts and top rods along the edges for railings, and checking fuel tank cylinder placement between the wheels and legs to avoid collisions with the hull side.

I'll put jerry cans and toolbox on one side and the tank on the other, placing the roundel decal in the free hull section between the leg beam and the wheel, and figuring out where to put the stencil markings on the rear face and turret side.

Now I'm settling on putting the stencil on the turret sides, the roundel on the hull, and a hazard strip along the turret bottom, with the fuel tank and toolboxes tucked in on the hull sides. Writing wheel placement logic...

Positioning the lug nuts correctly around each wheel, then adding spokes, skipping valve stems and brake discs for simplicity, and planning a merge helper to combine geometries by color. I still need to work out suspension components per axle (axles, springs, differential, steering tie rods) and define cable sweeps using catmull-rom curves.

Checking the sweep function signature for radius and side detail, then planning rails and posts using a rod helper—being careful about naming collisions between the builder object and parameters. I'm also working out the mast, a lathe-based dish antenna with a normalized axis direction, and a camera/EO turret mounted on the cab roof.

Now I'm setting up the gun pitch rotation matrix, verifying the trigonometry maps the barrel upward correctly, and defining helper functions to transform and place gun-local geometry through that matrix before building the textured gun plane.

I'm double-checking I only import the functions I actually use—createBuilder, paint, noise, mix, smoothstep, patches, svg, catmull—and skipping unused ones like a random jitter helper since nothing in this design calls for scattered noise effects.

Now I'm defining a tuple type for rotation parameters, then writing the fender geometry: angled boxes at each wheel well, rotated slightly around the x-axis so the front edge slopes downward while the rear tapers appropriately.

Adding more details...

Adding the dark bezel and glowing light boxes, then checking that the bumper at the nose's sloped bottom covers the area properly before finalizing all the geometry.
